props.statement: A hydrocarbon feedstock, a gas comprising hydrocarbons and/or hydrogen, and oxygen are reacted above 1200 °C so that cracking and combustion occur, giving acetylene, ethylene, methane, hydrogen, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide with a hydrogen:carbon monoxide volume ratio greater than 1:1; carbon dioxide, acetylene and ethylene are removed successively; the residual gas (methane, hydrogen, carbon monoxide) is converted catalytically to methanol at elevated temperature and pressure; the methanol produced is condensed and partly used to scrub the unreacted gas under pressure, and the methane dissolved in it is liberated on pressure release.

props.statement: A process for unsaturated hydrocarbons and methanol: (1) react a feedstock of hydrocarbons, hydrogen and oxygen above 1200 °C to a product containing acetylene, ethylene, methane, hydrogen, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide (printed: hydrocarbon:carbon monoxide volume ratio greater than 1:1); (2) remove successively carbon dioxide, acetylene and ethylene, leaving methane, hydrogen and carbon monoxide with hydrogen:carbon monoxide volume ratio greater than 1:1; (3) convert catalytically a substantial amount of hydrogen and carbon monoxide to methanol in a methanol converter; (4) condense the methanol and scrub the unreacted gases under elevated pressure with recycled product methanol, forming a solution of methane in methanol; (5) remove the solution, decrease its pressure and liberate the methane; (6) recycle product methanol to step (4); (7) recycle the scrubbed gases to the converter.
